# Tech Training

## Introduction

Tech Training is a free directory of audiovisual presentations for learning about technology and accessibility. Some people prefer to learn technology from demonstrations, webinars, podcasts, and other audio or video presentations rather than from electronic text alone; that preference inspired this project. Extensive collaboration between **Jamal Mazrui and ChatGPT** was used to search public sources, review and organize candidates, remove duplicates and material that was mainly promotional or noninstructional, and assemble the strongest results into one directory.

The current release contains **1304 unique presentations in 20 topic categories**. A presentation title links directly to the audio or video file, or to the actual free public presentation on a media host such as YouTube. No sign-in is required. Entries are limited to 2016 or later.

In this directory, a **source** is the person, organization, project, or publisher from whose collection a retained presentation was obtained; a source may operate more than one website, channel, podcast, or archive. The 25 sources below are sorted case-insensitively by substantive name, ignoring an initial `A`, `An`, or `The`. The number in parentheses is the count of presentations from that source.

- A. T. Guys (6)
- The Accessibility Guy (262)
- Accessible World (19)
- Adobe (11)
- American Foundation for the Blind (2)
- American Printing House for the Blind (58)
- AppleVis (498)
- AT3 Center (12)
- Blind Abilities (162)
- Blind Low Vision NZ (6)
- The Blind Podmaker (18)
- Dolphin Computer Access (20)
- Freedom Scientific (16)
- Google (5)
- inABLE (1)
- Jonathan Mosen (16)
- Microsoft (57)
- Minnesota STAR Program (2)
- National Federation of the Blind (8)
- National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (30)
- U.S. General Services Administration (61)
- University of Washington (12)
- Vision Australia (9)
- Vision-Aid (2)
- World Wide Web Consortium (11)

The presentation entries are organized for efficient browsing with a screen reader. Topic categories are at heading level 2, with the number of presentations shown in parentheses, and presentation titles are at heading level 3. Each category begins with a one-sentence definition. The year follows each presentation title so readers can quickly judge how current the material is. When reliable information is available, an entry also gives a concise description, listening time, presenter, series, source, and presentation-specific links such as transcripts, slides, or handouts. Listening times are rounded to the nearest minute.

Each presentation appears once in the best-fitting topic category. Titles and descriptions are normalized when that improves browsing or removes low-value boilerplate, while preserving substantive meaning. Individual email addresses and phone numbers are omitted. Five appendixes provide alternate browsing by year, source, presenter, series, and title.

The purpose of Tech Training is to make useful technology and accessibility instruction easier to discover and use without searching many separate websites, podcast archives, and video channels.
